input.quote: This Agreement will be governed by the substantive laws of the State of New York, without regard for its conflict of laws provisions.
input.rationale: § 14.3 selects New York substantive law, which is our preferred governing law, and the Agreement contains no arbitration provision (no hits for "arbitration") and no foreign venue, so there is no walk-away issue. However, the clause is silent on dispute forum — no section specifies venue or jurisdiction (only incidental "court of competent jurisdiction" references in §§ 8.2 and 14.5), and § 14.19 limits delivery to the United States without addressing forum. Because the preferred position requires exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, we added that forum language to the existing sentence, leaving the choice-of-law wording intact.

ops.oldText: This Agreement will be governed by the substantive laws of the State of New York, without regard for its conflict of laws provisions.
ops.newText: This Agreement will be governed by the substantive laws of the State of New York, without regard for its conflict of laws provisions. The parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York for any dispute arising out of or related to this Agreement.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] New York law is acceptable to us, but the clause is silent on forum, so we have added exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County to match the governing law and avoid disputes over venue.
proposal.summary: Add exclusive New York County court venue to the New York choice-of-law clause.
